proposal_text: The outcome Better teamwear delivery.Less repeated work. Make custom teamwear faster and easier to deliver, with a better experience for customers and the people doing the work. We will follow the journey from customer brief through design, revisions, approval and production handover. Simplify the process first, then use existing software, AI and automation where they can make a practical difference. An ambition to test: a complete customer brief becomes a compelling, realistic collection presentation within 48 hours. Discover will define eligible briefs and quality checks; the pilot will test the target. This is presentation time, not finished garment delivery. The approachDiscover. Design.Develop. Deliver.Understand the work, shape the improvement, prove it works and put it into everyday use. 01 | First engagementDiscoverWeek 1Understand the work and agree the priorities.Result: a shared view of the current workflow, its friction points and what success should look like.Next decision: agree the priority workflow, garment set and acceptance tests. 02 | First engagementDesignWeeks 2–3Make the improved experience tangible.Result: a reviewed clickable prototype, feasibility findings and a development plan.Next decision: accept the design work and decide whether to commission a working proof of concept. 03 | Later phaseDevelopSeparately approvedBuild and test a reliable working system.Result: a working proof, followed by a build and pilot on live customer briefs.Next decision: approve the build after the proof, then confirm the pilot passes the launch checks. 04 | Later phaseDeliverSeparately approvedHelp the team confidently use and own it.Result: training, editable assets and code, operating instructions and a named internal owner.Next decision: accept the handover and resolve critical defects before launch. Where we are nowA clear direction.Discover and Design come first.This proposal sets out the first engagement. The workflow, priorities and technical feasibility are still to be established through that work. Start with one real customer job.Follow a representative historical job from its original brief through revisions, approval and production handover. Use the real files and the team’s experience to answer three questions. What happens today?Map the people, files, tools, decisions and handovers. Where does the work get stuck?Find missing information, waiting, repeated effort and avoidable corrections. What should we improve first?Agree the most useful improvement and how we will measure its success. Design then turns the agreed priority workflow into a clickable prototype, with the screens needed to review it. Focused technical checks test the critical assumptions before we define the build. Investment and next stepBegin with Discover and Design. Combined fixed feeA$14,400 ex GSTThree delivery weeks.Four agreed outputs, detailed below. A$7,200 on signing the separate Project Management Agreement, before kickoff. A$7,200 on acceptance of Outputs 1–4. Invoices are payable within seven days; GST is added where applicable. To beginApprove the proposal in principle and complete the Project Management Agreement. Nominate the client lead and approver, select the historical job and confirm access. Agree kickoff once the commencement payment and required inputs are available. Develop and Deliver are separately scoped and approved after the findings. Their indicative allowances are included in the detailed scope. Review detailed scopeGo to proposal approval → Supporting detailScope, responsibilities and terms.These details form part of the proposal. Expand each section to review them; all sections are included when you save a PDF. Discover: workflow and requirementsOutputs 1–2 · Week 1 Output 1. Current workflow and evidenceOne prefilled questionnaire for up to four staff, one shared asset checklist and one 60-minute walkthrough with Jonny and Production. Sales joins the relevant part.Review one job across up to three styles. Produce the current workflow, including delays, repeated work, handovers and customer friction; an asset inventory; baseline evidence or a measurement plan; and gaps. The client lead confirms the findings. Output 2. Agreed requirements and testsRank improvements by customer value, time saved and practicality. Agree user needs, design-rule examples, the initial garment set and success measures. Use up to two 20-minute follow-ups only where material questions remain.The approver confirms the written scope and acceptance tests before detailed prototype work. Design: prototype and development planOutputs 3–4 · Weeks 2–3 Output 3. Prototype and feasibility evidenceA future workflow, a clickable prototype covering the agreed priority workflow, and comparison of existing software, configured integrations and a custom solution.Design and Production review the feasibility evidence, with demonstrated and unproven capabilities clearly distinguished. Assess options against quality, editability, compatibility, licensing, data handling and cost. Output 4. A defined development planOne 45-minute joint prototype review with up to three staff and one consolidated refinement.Produce review findings, recommended system structure, the scope and required checks for a working proof of concept, plus an indicative development budget and timetable. The final weekly review supports the next decision. Test the critical connections earlyUp to two focused technical checks, totalling eight consultant hours across Weeks 1–2, subject to usable files and licensed access. Prioritise editable artwork to accurate garment views and controlled changes across styles. The complete working proof of concept belongs to Develop and requires separate approval. Working together and accepting the workTeam input · Reviews · Commercial terms Focused team input Preparation: James drafts the workflow and requirements for staff to confirm. Role-specific questionnaires take approximately ten minutes per person, excluding file preparation. Existing approved tools can prefill, collate and flag gaps; James checks the synthesis before requirements are accepted. One shared job pack: the original brief, logos, editable Illustrator files, production files, final collection, revision history and available timings. One nominated owner coordinates the files. Staff time: allow an estimated 8–10 combined staff-hours across preparation, questionnaires, the walkthrough, prototype review and decisions. Ownership: Kate and Cam confirm the sponsors, one day-to-day lead, one commercial approver and Design and Production reviewers. Jonny is the proposed design counterpart. Reviews: one weekly 30-minute lead review and one shared decision log. Consolidated feedback within three business days; formal acceptance within five. Silence is not approval. AcceptanceAcceptance means complete, usable Outputs 1–4 against the descriptions above. One consolidated feedback round per deliverable and corrections to agreed scope are included. Record blockers and limitations; any material reduction or substitution needs written agreement. A supported recommendation to narrow the scope or stop is a valid result. Fee basis and changesThe fixed fee is based on 48 hours at A$300/hour, flexibly allocated across three delivery weeks. Extra effort needed to complete unchanged scope is not charged.Additional scope requires written approval at A$300/hour in 0.5-hour units, subject to a written cap. Software, API, hosting, specialist, travel and event costs are separate and need prior written approval. Existing client access is assumed; paid tests are quoted before commitment. Delayed inputs or decisions move the schedule. The workflow we will exploreCustomer experience · Safeguards · Boundaries Discover will establish which improvements deserve priority. The starting ideas are: Brief onceBring colours, logos, references, sponsors and garment choices into one brief. Explore extracting information from existing emails and files for staff to confirm. Develop conceptsCreate 3–5 starting directions using 776BC design rules, garment templates and approved assets. Build the collectionThe designer selects and refines a master direction, then applies its design language across the selected styles. Show it realisticallyPresent front, back and side garment views that accurately reflect editable artwork and garment construction. Revise consistentlyAssist changes across relevant artwork, garments and presentation views, with the designer checking the result. Approve and produceRecord the customer’s approved version and prepare editable production outputs for Design and Production release. Keep throughoutDesigner judgement, editable artwork, original logo geometry and garment constraints. Design and Production check work before customer or factory release. Customer assets are used with permission through approved services. Outside Discover and DesignAn operational system, live deployment or complete proof of concept; pattern drafting, grading, a full 3D library or major asset repair; a full design-library build, large migration or wider integrations; customer self-service and event implementation.The engagement includes a brief assessment of an existing-design 3D event showcase using Jordan’s written input where needed. Implementation is quoted separately; live logo personalisation remains a later opportunity. How we will measure successBaselines first · Pilot targets agreed together Speed to marketTime from an agreed complete brief to customer presentation, and from customer approval to production handover. Efficiency and capacityStaff hours, repeated tasks, waiting time and revision effort per comparable job. Customer experienceEase of briefing, reviewing and approving, using customer feedback and avoidable clarification rounds. Design and production qualityAdherence to design rules, accuracy between garment views and editable artwork, and production handovers accepted without correction. Commercial performanceQuote-to-order conversion, styles per order and average order value over a suitable period of live use. Agree baselines, measurement methods and pilot targets during Discover and Design. Conversion and order value are longer-term commercial measures. Develop and Deliver: indicative allowancesLater decisions · Separately scoped and approved These preliminary allowances support planning. Asset readiness and technical findings may materially change them. Later phaseTiming / effortFees, ex GST Develop: working proof, build and pilot8–11 weeks / 120–180 hoursA$36,000–54,000 Deliver: launch and handover2 weeks / 16–24 hoursA$4,800–7,200 Develop has two separate decisionsFirst, a working proof of concept: 3–4 weeks, A$12,000–18,000. Then build and pilot: 5–7 weeks, A$24,000–36,000. Each needs its own agreed scope and price.The working proof uses one historical rowing brief: three concepts on a master style, the chosen direction across two companion styles, front/back/side views and one controlled revision. Design and Production check quality, editability, accuracy and repeatability. The proposed live pilot then uses two designers and five suitable briefs, subject to volume, with the manual process retained as a fallback. Deliver includes ownership and handoverTraining, editable assets and bespoke code, account and recovery documentation, a named internal owner and accepted operating instructions. Review early results; ongoing support is separately agreed. Planning allowance across all four phases: A$55,200–75,600 over approximately 13–16 delivery weeks if consecutive. This is not an approved build budget. It excludes GST, third-party costs, specialists and event implementation.
